recipes.name: Chicken Karahi
recipes.description: A classic Pakistani chicken curry cooked in a wok-style karahi with tomatoes, ginger, and green chilies.
ingredients: Fresh coriander and ginger julienne for garnish
instructions: Heat oil in a karahi and add chicken, cooking on high heat until it changes color.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes, salt, and spices; cook until tomatoes break down and oil separates.
Add green chilies, cover, and simmer until chicken is tender.
Garnish with coriander and ginger, serve hot with naan or roti.

recipes.name: Daal Chawal
recipes.description: Simple everyday lentil curry served with steamed rice.
ingredients: 1 cup yellow lentils (masoor or chana daal)
instructions: Boil lentils with turmeric and salt until soft.
In a separate pan, heat oil and fry cumin seeds, then onions until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and tomatoes, cook until soft.
Pour this tempering into the boiled lentils and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with steamed basmati rice.

recipes.name: Beef Nihari
recipes.description: A slow-cooked, richly spiced beef stew traditionally eaten for breakfast.
ingredients: Ginger julienne, lemon, and coriander for garnish
instructions: Fry sliced onions in oil until golden brown, then set aside.
In the same oil, sear the beef, add nihari masala, and cook for a few minutes.
Add water to cover the meat and simmer on low heat for 3-4 hours until tender.
Mix wheat flour with water to make a slurry, stir into the stew to thicken.
Top with fried onions, ginger, coriander, and a squeeze of lemon before serving.

recipes.name: Vegetable Biryani
recipes.description: Fragrant layered rice dish cooked with mixed vegetables and biryani spices.
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (carrots, peas, potatoes, beans)
instructions: Parboil the rice with whole spices and salt until 70% cooked, then drain.
Cook mixed vegetables with yogurt, biryani masala, and half the fried onions until tender.
Layer the vegetable mixture and rice alternately in a pot, topping with mint, coriander, and remaining fried onions.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat (dum) for 20-25 minutes.
Gently mix before serving.
